newsitem.title: BOSNIA: UN demands ouster of radical Serb police chief.
newsitem.headline: UN demands ouster of radical Serb police chief.

text.p: NATO and the United Nations on Wednesday demanded the resignation of a Bosnian Serb police chief with a notorious past after he threatened peacekeepers with a banned assault weapon.

Simo Drljaca, police chief in the ultra-nationalist Serb district of Prijedor in northwest Bosnia, tops a list of "most abusive police officials in former Yugoslavia" compiled by the Human Rights Watch monitoring group.

Peter Fitzgerald, commissioner of U.N. police monitors in post-war Bosnia, met the interior minister of the separatist Serb entity on Wednesday to ask that he sack Drljaca within 48 hours, U.N. spokesman Alex Ivanko said.

Fitzgerald also demanded Prijedor municipality police turn over all long-barrelled assault weapons banned under demilitarisation provisions of the 1995 Dayton peace treaty signed by Serb, Moslem and Croat factions.

On Monday, Drljaca refused to hand over an MP-5 machine pistol to a Czech patrol of the NATO-led peace force (IFOR) and fired a shot into the air with it in an effort to make the Czech soldiers back off, an alliance spokesman said.
When they stood their ground, Drljaca called in 10 of his own policemen armed with banned AK-47 submachine guns to surround the Czechs.

"Mr Drljaca threatened IFOR soldiers by pointing the weapon at them and firing the weapon into the air. (Then) he ordered some of his policemen to intervene with illegal long-barrelled weapons," said IFOR spokesman Major Brett Boudreau.
"Mr Drljaca's actions represent contempt of the Dayton accord and his behaviour on this and earlier occasions has made his removal mandatory," Boudreau added.

Human Rights watch said Drljaca ran civil and paramilitary police units who helped Serb forces conquer the Prijedor area early in the war in 1992 and expel its local Moslem-Croat majority in brutal rounds of "ethnic cleansing".
"He was directly involved in setting up the infamous (concentration) camps around Prijedor as well," it said.
More recently, Drljaca has resisted cooperating with Fitzgerald's monitors who try to foster law-and-order and respect for human rights by local police throughout Bosnia.
"We believe enough is enough and he should probably call it a day and retire," Ivanko said.
Fitzgerald's U.N.-affiliated International Police Task Force has successfully obtained the removal of several other rogue police chiefs this year for gangsterism and assaults on minority civilians.
